airport.name: Capitán Av. Juan Cochamanidis S. Airport

summary: Capitán Av. Juan Cochamanidis S. Airport (SNG) is a small regional airport serving San Ignacio de Velasco, a historic town in the Santa Cruz Department of eastern Bolivia. The town is renowned for its well-preserved Jesuit Missions, which are part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site designation. The airport provides essential air connectivity to this remote lowland region, which is otherwise accessed by long overland journeys.
faqs:
Q: What is the airport code for Capitán Av. Juan Cochamanidis S. Airport?
A: The IATA code is SNG and the ICAO code is SLSI.

Q: What is the nearest town served by this airport?
A: San Ignacio de Velasco, a town in the Santa Cruz Department of Bolivia, is the primary destination served by this airport.

Q: Are there international flights at this airport?
A: No, this is a small regional airport that primarily handles domestic flights within Bolivia.

Q: What is San Ignacio de Velasco known for?
A: The town is famous for its 17th and 18th-century Jesuit mission churches, which are part of the Chiquitos Jesuit Missions UNESCO World Heritage Site.
transport_tips: The airport is located just a few kilometers from the town center of San Ignacio de Velasco, making transfers quick by taxi or moto-taxi. Given the limited scheduled service, passengers should confirm return flights in advance, as alternative ground transport to major cities like Santa Cruz can take 8-10 hours. Rental cars are generally not available at the airport, so arranging local transport through your hotel is recommended.
local_tip: Time your visit around the Festival Internacional de Música Renacentista y Barroca Americana, held every two years in San Ignacio, when historic mission music is performed in the restored Jesuit churches—book accommodations well in advance as the small town fills up quickly.
